clue.text: Greek youth setting record once with cupholder

parts.note: EP, an extended-play record, was a format of the past
Hebe was cupbearer to the Greek gods, so she held their cups

explanation.surface: A Greek lad sets a record while carrying a cup for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text drops the c of 'cupholder'; the page prints it whole. An EP is an old record format, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a young man entering adulthood and military training bore this title.

clue.text: Globe-fish is enough for a mundane chap

parts.note: the globe is the earth
a ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A puffer fish is more than enough for an ordinary fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Globe-fish' reads as one fish; split it. 'Mundane' is literal: of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Mundane means of this world, and an inhabitant of our planet is exactly that.

clue.text: Wasted writer

definitions.meaning: gaunt and worn, as from illness or worry
H. Rider ..., author of King Solomon's Mines

explanation.surface: An author has drunk too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaunt from strain fits one sense; the other is the Victorian adventure novelist.

clue.text: Like flier representing US. having no regard for the consequences

definitions.meaning: the bald eagle, emblem of the United States, has a white head

definitions.text: having no regard for the consequences
definitions.meaning: to go at something in this way is to charge in recklessly

explanation.surface: A bird symbolising America behaves recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The bald eagle is not hairless but white-headed; the second sense is an old idiom for rushing in headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking hair on top describes the eagle; going at it so means plunging ahead rashly.

clue.text: Sailor's in the drink!

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor, and the 's stays as S
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shouts that a seaman has fallen overboard into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, so the surface reads as a cry of man overboard; the exclamation mark flags the double reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A green aniseed-flavoured spirit flavoured with wormwood is one kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Mrs. Cripps, though, has wrong cruet with pepper at first

parts.note: but and though both concede a point

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of cruet are put into a different order
at first says only the opening letter of pepper is used

explanation.surface: A woman with a cruet set has got the pepper the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Cripps is Little Buttercup, the bumboat woman in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore. 'Wrong' turns CRUET into TERCU.
explanation.definitionFit: In the operetta the portly dockside vendor Mrs Cripps goes by the nickname of this yellow flower.

clue.text: He has the bed-head removed

indicators.note: head removed says the first letter is taken off the word for bed

parts.note: a divan is a kind of bed

explanation.surface: A man has had the headboard taken off his bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed-head' is one word in the surface; the bed is DIVAN and its head, D, is removed. 'He' is a male name, like Ivan.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian man's name, and Russians are sometimes jokingly called by it, so a man.

clue.text: God, I see it's said, is great

parts.note: the Titans were Greek gods, older than the Olympians
taken as written

indicators.note: it's said says the word before it is heard spoken, giving a letter of the same sound

parts.note: see said aloud is the letter C

explanation.surface: A believer declares that God is great.
explanation.definitionFit: Something colossal or gigantic is enormous in scale.

clue.text: Panic after first losing shirt, sort of? That's a mistake

indicators.note: after first losing says the opening letter of the word for panic is dropped

parts.note: terror is extreme panic
a T-shirt is a sort of shirt, so T

explanation.surface: Someone frets about losing their shirt and admits it was a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or slip is a fault in judgment or fact.

clue.text: Happily unaffected when ends are switched

indicators.note: ends names the letters at the start and finish of the word for unaffected as the ones to move
are switched says those letters change places with each other in the word

parts.note: naif means naive, natural and unaffected

explanation.surface: Someone is cheerfully untroubled once the ends change over.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the N and F at the ends of NAIF.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning gladly or willingly, as in I would fain go.

clue.text: Knock back first class beer in the Crown and Sceptre, say

indicators.note: to knock back is to drink, but here it says the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class, its digit standing as the letter I
lager is a beer

explanation.surface: Someone downs a top-quality pint in a pub called the Crown and Sceptre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' turns A1 plus LAGER around to give REGAL1A. 'The Crown and Sceptre' looks like a pub name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown and sceptre are among the royal emblems and insignia worn or carried by a monarch.

clue.text: To flower, it turns brown

parts.note: taken as written
an aster is a flower

explanation.surface: A plant comes into bloom and its petals go brown.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text has a stray I at the start; the page prints none. 'Flower' is a noun here, not the verb the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen appliance browns slices of bread with heat.

clue.text: One who works for a capitation fee?

definitions.text: One who works for a capitation fee?

parts.words: One who works for a capitation fee?
parts.note: a capitation fee is a charge per head; read literally, someone paid per head collected, like a recruiter or a tribal trophy-taker

explanation.surface: A professional paid a fixed amount per person on their books.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruiter who poaches executives for a fee, or a warrior collecting skulls, is paid by heads.

clue.text: Protuberance in the back row

indicators.note: back says the word for row is turned to read the other way

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers

explanation.surface: Something sticks out in the back row of seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the' is a link; 'back' reverses RANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot or gnarl on a tree trunk is a lump that sticks out.

clue.text: Articulated to make clear

definitions.meaning: marked or very noticeable, as a strong accent

explanation.surface: Speaking in order to make things plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To make' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A word spoken aloud is uttered; a distinct, marked feature is obvious.

clue.text: Pulled in for lottery in pub

indicators.note: in says one word goes inside the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a draw is a lottery

explanation.surface: Someone is lured into a pub to buy a raffle ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: Breath that is drawn inward has been taken in or sucked in.

clue.text: New hearing device making a bit of a squeak

parts.note: an ear is the thing we hear with, so ear plus thing

explanation.surface: A new hearing aid starts to squeal a little.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'narrow squeak' is a lucky escape, so 'a bit of a squeak' is a close shave. The device is jokily an 'ear thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A close call or narrow escape is a narrow squeak, a lucky miss.

clue.text: Sort of pipe in middle of the ear

definitions.meaning: a tobacco pipe whose bowl is made from a dried maize cob
the central woody core of a maize ear, to which the kernels attach

explanation.surface: A kind of tube is found deep inside the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the ear on your head; it is an ear of maize.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of maize is the cob, and dried ones are hollowed into tobacco pipes.

clue.text: Large cloth for a dorm feast

definitions.meaning: a big covering laid over a bed
a spread is a feast, and in a dormitory one could be set out on a bed

explanation.surface: A big tablecloth is laid out for a midnight feast in the dormitory.
explanation.definitionFit: A coverlet is a big cover for a bed; a meal laid out on bedding is a bed spread.

clue.text: One expected to shoot — a large-leaved plant

parts.note: a gunner is a soldier whose job is firing guns

explanation.surface: A marksman is introduced alongside a plant with big leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text splits 'large-leaved' with a comma; the page prints it hyphenated. 'Shoot' hints at plant growth but means firing.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American perennial is known for enormous rhubarb-like foliage.

clue.text: Endless fight at sea for a meat dish

indicators.note: endless says the last letter of the name of the sea fight is lost

parts.note: Navarino, 1827, was a naval battle in the Greek War of Independence

explanation.surface: An unending naval battle is fought over a plate of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A French ragout of lamb or mutton stewed with root vegetables.

clue.text: Doctor in operation going round holding a small knife

indicators.note: holding says the turned run takes a letter inside it
going round says the doctor, in and operation pieces are turned to read the other way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A surgeon in theatre does the rounds carrying a little blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' reverses DRINOP to PONIRD, which then holds A. The surface's operating theatre and doctor are a decoy for abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A dagger is a slender blade for stabbing, a short weapon.

clue.text: Old monk vinegary about saint

indicators.note: about says the word for vinegary goes around the saint

parts.note: acetic means of or like vinegar

explanation.surface: An elderly monk turns sour about a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Early hermits who practised severe self-denial in the desert were the original monks of austerity.

clue.text: Bar codes a vegetable displays

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A barcode is shown on a vegetable at the supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar codes' reads as one thing, but 'Bar' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar and save both mean except, as in all bar one.

clue.text: Formal body

explanation.surface: A ceremonial organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy manners are rigid; a dead body is slang called this.

clue.text: Drink up!

parts.note: read as an instruction to finish a glass, but also a drink taken while up on horseback

explanation.surface: A host urges the company to finish their glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: A parting glass handed to a rider already mounted is taken while up in the saddle.

clue.text: Is it right to turn up single here in the US?

indicators.note: to turn up says, in a down entry, that the word for single is read upwards

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether it is proper for an unmarried person to show up somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Reno, Nevada, was famous for quick divorces, so a place one becomes single again.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nevada city is a location in the United States.

clue.text: Book with one bit of Greek text or another

parts.note: eta is one of the letters of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A volume containing a snippet of Greek or some other language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or another' means another Greek letter, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Greek alphabet is another such character beside eta.

clue.text: Hands, for example, to one national

parts.note: Israel Hands is the pirate coxswain in Stevenson's Treasure Island
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A list of hands is given to a single citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' looks like workers but is the surname of Israel Hands from Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the Jewish state in the Middle East is one of its nationals.

clue.text: Embrace link an American may take to be formal

definitions.text: an American may take to be formal

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
a tie is a link or bond

explanation.surface: A hug is a connection that someone from the US may think is stiff and proper.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans use this word where Britons say simply tie, worn with formal dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth knotted at the collar is what US speakers call this smart item of clothing.

clue.text: Excite tribesman to perform dance

parts.note: to fan flames or feelings is to excite them
Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, so a Danite tribesman
to go can mean to perform or function, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a member of a tribe to put on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Spanish courtship number in triple time, danced with castanets.

clue.text: Editor accepts leader is drawn out

indicators.note: accepts says the editor takes the leader inside

parts.note: Il Duce, Italian for the leader, was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor agrees that their chief has been dragged out.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to elicit or bring out something latent.
